ja.L: それゆえ、イスラエルよ、わたしはあなたにこのようにする。 \q わたしがあなたにこのことをするのだから、 \q イスラエルよ、あなたの神に会う備えをせよ。
ja.B: だから、イスラエルよ、わたしはあなたにこうする。 \q わたしがこのことをあなたにするのだから、 \q イスラエルよ、あなたの神に会う備えをしなさい。
ja.R: だから、イスラエルよ、わたしはあなたにこうする。 \q わたしがこれをあなたにするのだから、 \q イスラエルよ、あなたの神に会う用意をしなさい。

decisions.choice: thus I will do to you: what the LORD will do is not said
decisions.reason: "Thus" and "this" usually point to something said next, but nothing follows. The LORD leaves the threat open, which makes it more fearful than any description. Some take "this" to point back to the judgments already announced (3:11-15; 4:2-3), others forward to the meeting with God in the same verse.

decisions.choice: prepare to meet your God: the words of Sinai, now a summons to judgment
decisions.reason: At Sinai the people were told to "be ready", and Moses brought them out "to meet God" (Exodus 19:11, 15, 17). Israel will meet its God again, but after five refusals to return (verses 6-11) the meeting will be for judgment. Some hear in the words a last call to repent before that meeting, but the verse itself announces it.

decisions.choice: O Israel (L), Israel (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal marks the calling out of Israel's name with "O", as in Hosea; Balanced and Readable use the name alone. Readable says "get ready" for "prepare".

decisions.choice: tú to Israel
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew speaks to Israel in the singular, as one person, so Spanish uses tú and no plural_you span.

decisions.choice: "te", "ton": Israël in the singular
decisions.reason: After the plural of verses 4-11, the Hebrew speaks to Israel as one person, and French follows its number.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" for Israel addressed as one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from the plural "you" of verses 6-11 to the singular, Israel as one person summoned before God; "ngươi" keeps that, as the rebuke address of the terms sheet.

decisions.choice: Preparem-se para encontrar o seu Deus (vocês)
alternatives: Prepara-te para encontrar o teu Deus (tu)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here, Israel called by name as one, and Portuguese could say "tu". It keeps "vocês", the address of verses 4-11 to the same people, so that the summons does not seem to turn to someone new, and so that the line reads as a call to every hearer. The words recall Sinai, where the people prepared to meet God (m2).

decisions.choice: Israel addressed as "አንተ" ("አደርግብሃለሁ", "አምላክህን", "ተዘጋጅ")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from the plural of verses 4-11 to the masculine singular, the nation as one person summoned to meet its God; Amharic can keep the change, English cannot.

decisions.choice: приготовься встретить (L); готовься встретить (B); готовься встретиться (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Sinai (meaning decision), now a summons to judgment; the imperative of readiness is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: Israel addressed in the singular "あなた" here (the Hebrew turns to the singular); hikkon "備えをせよ" (L), "備えをしなさい" (B), "用意をしなさい" (R).
decisions.reason: One people as one あなた (ISA, HOS address rule).

source.text: כִּ֡י הִנֵּה֩ יוֹצֵ֨ר הָרִ֜ים וּבֹרֵ֣א ר֗וּחַ וּמַגִּ֤יד לְאָדָם֙ מַה־שֵּׂח֔וֹ עֹשֵׂ֥ה שַׁ֨חַר֙ עֵיפָ֔ה וְדֹרֵ֖ךְ עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי אָ֑רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For look, [the one] forming mountains and creating wind, and declaring to humankind what [is] his thought, making dawn darkness, and treading on [the] heights of [the] earth: Yahweh, God of hosts, [is] his name.

en.L: For look, the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to humankind what {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} thought [is], \q who makes the dawn darkness, \q and treads on the earth's heights: \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who reveals {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} thoughts to humankind, \q who turns the dawn into darkness \q and treads on the heights of the earth: \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: He formed the mountains and created the wind. He tells people what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is planning. \q He turns the dawn into darkness \q and walks on the high places of the earth. \q His name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies.

es.L: Porque he aquí, el que forma los montes y crea el viento, y declara al ser humano cuál [es] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pensamiento, \q el que hace de la aurora tinieblas, \q y camina sobre las alturas de la tierra: \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos [es] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.B: Porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es quien forma los montes y crea el viento, quien revela a la humanidad {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pensamientos, \q quien convierte la aurora en tinieblas \q y camina sobre las alturas de la tierra: \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.R: Él formó los montes y creó el viento. Él les dice a los seres humanos lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} piensa hacer. \q Él convierte el amanecer en oscuridad \q y camina sobre los lugares altos de la tierra. \q Su nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Car voici, celui qui forme les montagnes et crée le vent, et qui révèle {{gender:à l’être humain|à l’homme}} quelle [est] {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} pensée, \q qui fait de l’aurore les ténèbres, \q et marche sur les hauteurs de la terre : \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, [est] {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.B: Car c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui forme les montagnes et crée le vent, qui fait connaître {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pensées {{gender:aux humains|aux hommes}}, \q qui change l’aurore en ténèbres \q et marche sur les hauteurs de la terre : \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.R: Il a formé les montagnes et créé le vent. Il dit aux gens ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a l’intention de faire. \q Il change l’aurore en ténèbres \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} marche sur les hauteurs de la terre. \q Son nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aiumbaye milima na kuuumba upepo, na kumjulisha mwanadamu wazo {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} [ni] nini, \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aifanyaye alfajiri kuwa giza, \q na kukanyaga mahali palipoinuka pa dunia: \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi [ndilo] jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye aiumbaye milima na kuuumba upepo, anayewafunulia wanadamu mawazo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q anayeigeuza alfajiri kuwa giza \q na kukanyaga juu ya vilele vya dunia: \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi ndilo jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.R: Yeye aliifanya milima na kuuumba upepo. Huwaambia watu mipango {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Huigeuza alfajiri kuwa giza \q na kutembea juu ya vilele vya dunia. \q Jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi.

vi.L: Vì này, Đấng tạo nên núi non và dựng nên gió, và bày tỏ cho loài người biết ý tưởng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q Đấng biến rạng đông thành tối tăm, \q và bước đi trên các nơi cao của đất: \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân [là] danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Đấng tạo nên núi non và dựng nên gió, Đấng bày tỏ ý tưởng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho loài người, \q Đấng biến rạng đông thành tối tăm \q và bước đi trên các nơi cao của đất: \q danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân.
vi.R: Ngài đã tạo nên núi non và dựng nên gió. Ngài cho loài người biết điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang dự định. \q Ngài biến bình minh thành bóng tối \q và bước đi trên những nơi cao của đất. \q Danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân.

ko.L: 보라, 산들을 지으시고 바람을 창조하시며, 그분의 생각이 무엇인지 사람에게 알리시는 분, \q 새벽을 어둠으로 바꾸시고, \q 땅의 높은 곳들을 밟으시는 분, \q 그분의 이름은 만군의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}이시다.
ko.B: 그분은 산들을 지으시고 바람을 창조하시며, 그분의 생각을 사람에게 알려 주시는 분, \q 새벽을 어둠으로 바꾸시고 \q 땅의 높은 곳들을 밟고 다니시는 분이다. \q 그분의 이름은 만군의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}이시다.
ko.R: 그분은 산들을 만드시고 바람을 지으셨다. 그분은 사람들에게 그분의 계획을 알려 주신다. \q 새벽을 어둠으로 바꾸시고 \q 땅의 높은 곳들을 걸어 다니신다. \q 그분의 이름은 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}이시다.

pt.L: Pois eis que aquele que forma os montes e cria o vento, e declara ao ser humano qual [é] o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} pensamento, \q que faz da aurora escuridão, \q e pisa sobre as alturas da terra: \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos Exércitos, [é] o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} nome.
pt.B: Pois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é quem forma os montes e cria o vento, quem revela à humanidade os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pensamentos, \q quem transforma a aurora em escuridão \q e pisa sobre as alturas da terra: \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos Exércitos, é o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} nome.
pt.R: Ele formou os montes e criou o vento. Ele conta às pessoas o que está planejando. \q Ele transforma a manhã em escuridão \q e anda sobre os lugares altos da terra. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos Exércitos, é o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} nome.

am.L: እነሆ፣ ተራሮችን የሚሠራ፣ ነፋስንም የሚፈጥር፣ አሳቡንም ለሰው የሚገልጥ፣ \q ንጋትን ጨለማ የሚያደርግ፣ \q በምድርም ከፍታዎች ላይ የሚረግጥ፤ \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የጸባኦት አምላክ ስሙ [ነው]።
am.B: እርሱ ተራሮችን የሚሠራ፣ ነፋስንም የሚፈጥር፣ አሳቡንም ለሰው የሚገልጥ ነው፤ \q ንጋትን ወደ ጨለማ የሚለውጥ፣ \q በምድር ከፍታዎች ላይ የሚራመድ ነው፤ \q ስሙ የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ነው።
am.R: ተራሮችን የሠራ፣ ነፋስንም የፈጠረ እርሱ ነው። የሚያቅደውን ለሰዎች ይነግራቸዋል። \q ንጋትን ጨለማ ያደርጋል፤ \q በምድር ከፍታዎች ላይ ይራመዳል። \q ስሙ የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ነው።

hi.L: क्योंकि देखो, जो पहाड़ों को रचते और पवन को सृजते हैं, और मनुष्य पर प्रकट करते हैं कि उनका विचार क्या [है], \q जो भोर को अंधकार बनाते हैं, \q और पृथ्वी के ऊँचे स्थानों पर चलते हैं: \q {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, सेनाओं के परमेश्वर, उनका नाम [है]।
hi.B: क्योंकि वे ही पहाड़ों को रचनेवाले और पवन को सृजनेवाले हैं, जो मनुष्यों पर अपने विचार प्रकट करते हैं, \q जो भोर को अंधकार में बदल देते हैं \q और पृथ्वी के ऊँचे स्थानों पर चलते हैं: \q {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, सेनाओं के परमेश्वर, उनका नाम है।
hi.R: उन्होंने पहाड़ों को बनाया और पवन को रचा। वे लोगों को बताते हैं कि उनकी योजना क्या है। \q वे भोर को अंधकार में बदल देते हैं \q और पृथ्वी के ऊँचे स्थानों पर चलते हैं। \q उनका नाम {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, सेनाओं के परमेश्वर है।

ru.L: Ведь вот, образующий горы и творящий ветер, и возвещающий человеку, какова {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} мысль, \q делающий зарю тьмою \q и ступающий по высотам земли: \q {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Саваоф, — имя {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.
ru.B: Ведь {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} — тот, кто образует горы и творит ветер, кто открывает людям свои замыслы, \q кто превращает зарю во тьму \q и ступает по высотам земли: \q {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Саваоф, — {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} имя.
ru.R: Он создал горы и сотворил ветер. Он говорит людям, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} задумал. \q Он превращает утро во тьму \q и ходит по высотам земли. \q Его имя — {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Воинств.

ja.L: まことに、見なさい、山々を形づくり、風を創造し、人にご自分の思いが何であるかを告げ、 \q 暁を闇とし、 \q 地の高い所を踏まれる方、 \q その名は万軍の神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}。
ja.B: まことに、山々を形づくり、風を創造し、ご自分の思いを人に明かされる方、 \q 暁を闇に変え、 \q 地の高い所を踏み行かれる方、 \q その名は万軍の神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}。
ja.R: その方は、山々を造り、風を造られた。ご自分の計画を、人々に知らせてくださる。 \q その方は、夜明けを暗闇に変え、 \q 地の高い所を歩まれる。 \q その方の名は、天の軍勢を率いる神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}だ。

decisions.choice: a hymn to the Creator: the God whom Israel must meet
decisions.reason: The verse is a short hymn: a string of descriptions of God ("who forms ... who creates ... who treads") closing with "the LORD God of hosts is his name". Similar hymns stand in 5:8-9 and 9:5-6. It answers verse 12: the God Israel must prepare to meet is the maker of mountains and wind, who rules the whole earth.

decisions.choice: wind: the wind, created by God
decisions.reason: The word can mean wind, breath or spirit. Beside "mountains" it means the wind, part of the created world (Psalm 135:7; Jeremiah 10:13).

decisions.choice: declares to humankind what his thought is: God makes his own purpose known
alternatives: he shows a person his own thoughts
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "what his thought is", and "his" could be God or the person. Most likely God makes his own plans known to people, as he reveals his secret to the prophets (3:7). It can also mean that God shows a person his own hidden thoughts (Psalm 139:2; Jeremiah 11:20).

decisions.choice: who makes the dawn darkness: he turns morning into darkness
alternatives: who makes the dawn and the darkness
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side without "and". They can mean that God turns dawn into darkness, as in the judgment of 5:8 and 8:9, or that he makes both dawn and darkness, the order of day and night.

decisions.choice: treads on the heights of the earth: the LORD strides over the world as its ruler
decisions.reason: Micah 1:3 uses the same words of the LORD coming down in judgment; Deuteronomy 32:13 and Job 9:8 speak of treading on the heights in the same way. To tread on a place is to rule it.

decisions.choice: the LORD God of hosts (L), the LORD God of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: Where Amos joins "God of hosts" directly to the divine name, the wording is "the LORD God of hosts" at Literal and "the LORD God of Armies" at Balanced and Readable, as in the Psalms (Psalm 80:5; 84:9) and in Amos 5:14-16, 27; 6:8, 14. On the title, see 3:13. Balanced and Readable turn the descriptions into clauses about God ("he is the one who", "He formed"), and Readable puts his name at the end in its own sentence.

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR Dios de los ejércitos" (L); "de los Ejércitos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for "the LORD God of hosts", with no comma.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân" at every level
alternatives: "CHÚA Đức Chúa Trời của các đạo binh"
decisions.reason: "The LORD God of hosts" is the divine-name span followed by a comma and "Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân", as 1 Kings 19:10 and the terms sheet give it. Recorded once for Amos.

decisions.choice: The hymn speaks about God with -시- and "그분"; "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}이시다" closes it
decisions.reason: A hymn to the Creator in the third person; Korean gives it the honorific, as the English has deity_pronoun spans. "The LORD God of hosts" is "만군의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}" (L, B), "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}" (R), as the Psalms.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:à l'être humain|à l'homme}}" (L); "{{gender:aux humains|aux hommes}}" (B)
decisions.reason: Adam here is humankind; French has two wordings, so it carries the gender setting where the English "humankind" needs none. Readable says "aux gens".

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR, Dieu des armées" at every level
alternatives: "le SEIGNEUR Dieu des armées" without the comma
decisions.reason: The French form for "the LORD God of hosts" in the Twelve.

decisions.choice: O SENHOR, o Deus dos Exércitos, é o seu nome ([é] at Literal)
alternatives: O seu nome é SENHOR Deus dos Exércitos
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the close of the three hymns (4:13; 5:8-9; 9:5-6) keeps one wording at every level, with the Hebrew order, the name first: "O SENHOR, o Deus dos Exércitos, é o seu nome", and "O SENHOR é o seu nome" where the Hebrew has the divine name alone (5:8; 9:6). Readable keeps it too, so that the refrain is heard as one, rather than the English Readable's "His name is". "O Deus dos Exércitos" as at 3:13.

decisions.choice: ao ser humano
decisions.reason: The word means humankind (m3); "o ser humano" says it without a gender setting, which the English does not use here either.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, सेनाओं के परमेश्वर, उनका नाम है
decisions.reason: Where Amos joins "God of hosts" to the divine name, Hindi keeps the name first and the title after it, with सेनाओं के परमेश्वर as in 3:13. The same closing line returns in 5:8, 5:27 and 9:6. The Creator is spoken of with honorific forms.

decisions.choice: ГОСПОДЬ, Бог Саваоф (L, B); ГОСПОДЬ, Бог Воинств (R)
decisions.reason: "God of hosts" as in 3:13.

decisions.choice: The hymn (also 5:8-9, 9:5-6) speaks of God in the third person with light respect forms (踏まれる, 明かされる, 歩まれる) and closes on the name: YHWH 'elohei tseva'ot shemo "その名は万軍の神、主" (L, B), "その方の名は、天の軍勢を率いる神、主だ" (R); bara' "創造する" (L, B), "造る" (R).
decisions.reason: OT poetry rule for God in the third person; the title as 2 Samuel 5:10 and 1 Kings (万軍の神、主).
